Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: mathiasdan123
Message:
Add structured PDMS-2 scoring workflow with basal/ceiling automation (#378)

Builds the item-level PDMS-2 scoring workflow Megan specced into the
outcome-measures feature:

- shared/pdms2.ts: pure scoring logic shared by client (live indicators)
  and server (authoritative compute) — six subtest definitions (counts and
  age applicability only), basal detection with auto-credits, ceiling
  detection with exclusion of items above it, credited raw-score math,
  age-based domain-sum selection (Reflexes vs Object Manipulation at the
  12-month boundary), standard descriptive bands, zod shapes.
- New pdms2_assessments table (additive; sparse item scores, computed
  scoring state, manual normative-table entries, quotients, notes,
  narrative; scoped to patient + practice).
- server: pdms2ScoringService (recomputes state on every save),
  pdms2NarrativeService (AI draft from entered scores + therapist notes
  only, anti-fabrication charter, therapist edits and decides),
  /api/pdms2-assessments routes with tenant guards, storage module.
- client: Pdms2ScoringWorkflow component in the outcome-measures page —
  keyboard-fast 0/1/2 item grids, live basal/ceiling indicators, raw-score
  display, "from your PDMS-2 Examiner's Manual" manual-entry fields with
  interpretation bands, quotient sums to look up, editable AI narrative.

Copyright boundary: no PDMS-2 normative tables, item text, or mastery
criteria anywhere — the system records scores and automates arithmetic;
all conversions are manual lookups in the therapist's own manual.

Tests: 42 scoring-service unit tests + 7 client workflow tests.

Co-authored-by: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: mathiasdan123
Message:
Add Stedi Claim Lifecycle API client and read-only claims view endpoint (#336)

First slice of the Claim Lifecycle integration (API went GA 2026-09-09):
a typed client for GET /claims (statuses through adjudication, paid
amounts once the 835 lands, keyed by patientControlNumber = platform
claim id) and GET /api/claims/lifecycle exposing it to financial-role
users. Applies the ERA-poller lessons: 404 never impersonates an empty
list, and an empty page ends pagination regardless of returned tokens.

Deliberately read-only: platform claim statuses are NOT rewritten from
lifecycle data yet — that mapping (coarse lifecycle states vs the
277-based reaper's, no status regressions on reconciled claims) is a
follow-up product decision before any automatic sync.

Co-authored-by: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: mathiasdan123
Message:
fix(privacy): stop shipping live portal tokens to Sentry (#269)

Sentry's beforeSend scrubbed cookies, request bodies, query strings and the
Authorization header — but never request.url. Portal magic links carry the
token as a PATH segment (/patient-portal/login/<64 hex>), so a live
credential to a patient's chart was being sent to a vendor that is NOT
covered by the BAA. Anyone with Sentry read access could copy it out of an
issue and open the chart.

Traces were worse. beforeSend runs on ERROR events only, and traces are
sampled separately at 20% in production, so roughly a fifth of all portal
requests carried their token straight past the scrubber even when nothing
went wrong.

- shared/redactSensitiveUrl: replaces token-like path segments (24+ hex), the
  segment following login/join/token/magic-link/reset, and the values of
  credential-bearing query keys. Lives in shared/ so the server and browser
  bundles cannot drift — a token redacted on one side and leaked from the
  other is the same breach. It never throws; a redaction helper that can
  throw would take out the error reporter itself.
- Applied to event.request.url and event.transaction in beforeSend, and in a
  new beforeSendTransaction on both server and client.
- Client breadcrumbs also carry the fetched URL; redacted there too.

Tests: magic-link paths (server and client routes), telehealth join codes and
?token= values are redacted; ordinary paths, short numeric ids and
parameterised routes are left intact; junk input does not throw.

Co-authored-by: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
